name: Bachelor of Business (Accounting)
description:
The Accounting specialisation at ICMS sits on the same core 12-subject business spine as the college's other Bachelor of Business streams, then adds the technical accounting sequence (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation and corporate finance) needed to satisfy the professional accreditation requirements of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ. Getting that accreditation lined up matters more for accounting than for most other business majors, since it directly gates the pathway into the CA or CPA program after graduation, and ICMS structures the specialisation units specifically against those bodies' unit requirements.

Like every ICMS undergraduate degree, the course folds in two Work Integrated Learning placements totalling up to 600 hours, which for accounting students commonly means time inside a mid-tier or boutique Sydney accounting firm rather than a classroom-only capstone. That's a meaningful differentiator against accounting majors at universities where the professional placement is optional or informally arranged, since ICMS builds relationships with firms directly and treats the placement as a graded, credit-bearing part of the degree.

Graduates typically head toward roles in public practice, corporate accounting or financial analysis, with the accreditation pathway keeping CA/CPA progression open without needing a separate postgraduate conversion course.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Accounting Fundamentals; Economics for Managers; Business Law; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Business Statistics
Level 200: Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Corporate Finance; Company Law; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Auditing and Assurance; Taxation Law and Practice; Advanced Financial Reporting; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (professional placement)

name: Bachelor of Business (Marketing)
description:
ICMS runs its business degrees on a shared structural template: 12 core business subjects everyone takes regardless of specialisation, then a run of specialisation subjects, electives and two Work Integrated Learning placements bolted on. The Marketing stream slots into that frame with brand strategy, digital marketing and consumer behaviour content layered over the core management, economics and accounting units. The core subjects include named units like Pathway to Success and Unlocking Your Leadership Potential, which signals ICMS's employability-first pitch: these aren't abstract theory units but built around workplace-readiness skills from day one.

What differentiates ICMS's Marketing degree from a marketing major buried inside a big university's commerce degree is the WIL component: up to two trimesters, roughly nine months, of supervised professional placement built directly into the award. For marketing specifically, that tends to mean students working inside agency, retail or hospitality marketing teams around Sydney, given ICMS's strong existing placement relationships in the tourism and hospitality sector it was originally built around.

The Manly campus itself, a heritage sandstone building overlooking Manly Beach that students and staff refer to as 'the castle on the hill', gives the degree an unusually pleasant physical setting relative to most CBD-based business schools, something that comes up repeatedly in student reviews and open day materials.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing Principles; Economics for Managers; Accounting Fundamentals; Creativity and Innovation for Business
Level 200: Consumer Behaviour; Digital Marketing; Brand Management; Marketing Research; two further core/specialisation units; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Marketing; Integrated Marketing Communications; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (professional placement)

name: Bachelor of Business (Property)
description:
ICMS's Property specialisation is a newer addition to its business degree suite, built to feed Sydney's persistently active property and construction sector, a market where demand for graduates with both business fundamentals and property-specific knowledge (valuation, property law, development finance, asset management) has stayed strong even through broader graduate market softness elsewhere. It sits on the standard ICMS core-subjects spine before specialising into property valuation, real estate law, property development and funds/asset management units.

The Work Integrated Learning placements (up to 600 hours across two subjects) commonly place students with real estate agencies, property funds, valuation firms or development companies around Sydney, giving graduates direct exposure to a sector where a large share of hiring still runs through personal networks and internship-to-hire pathways rather than open graduate programs.

Because the specialisation is smaller and newer than ICMS's hospitality-heritage degrees, cohort sizes tend to be modest, which in practice means closer staff-student contact and more individualised placement matching than a large-university property degree with hundreds of students competing for the same handful of industry placements.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Accounting Fundamentals; Business Law
Level 200: Property Valuation; Real Estate Law; Property Development; Asset and Funds Management; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Property Management; Urban Planning and Development Economics; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (property industry placement)

name: Bachelor of Business (Sports Management)
description:
ICMS built its Sports Management degree around Sydney's genuine concentration of professional sport, and the college's placement network reflects that: students on this stream commonly end up placed with NRL and A-League clubs, stadium operators, or sports marketing agencies for their Work Integrated Learning component, rather than generic corporate placements. Content covers sports marketing, event operations and sponsorship alongside the standard ICMS core business subjects (economics, accounting, management, leadership), so graduates come out with a genuine business qualification rather than a narrower sport science credential.

The degree follows ICMS's usual 12 core, several specialisation, elective and two-WIL-subject structure, with sports-specific units layered into the specialisation slots. Sponsorship and commercial partnerships, facility and stadium management, and sports event logistics feature prominently given how much of Sydney's major-event calendar (State of Origin, international cricket, A-League finals) runs through venues the college has existing relationships with.

Students interested in athlete management, club administration or major event delivery tend to gravitate here rather than to ICMS's separate Event Management degree, though there's meaningful elective overlap between the two given how closely sports and events management skillsets sit together in the Australian industry.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing Principles; Economics for Managers; Introduction to Sport Management
Level 200: Sports Marketing and Sponsorship; Sport Event Management; Facility and Stadium Management; Consumer Behaviour; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Sport Business; Sport Governance and Policy; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (placement with a sporting organisation)

name: Bachelor of Event Management
description:
ICMS markets this degree hard on rankings, and the underlying substance backs some of that up: the college has deep placement relationships across Sydney's events calendar, from Vivid Sydney to major conference and exhibition venues, which feeds directly into the course's Work Integrated Learning placements. The core business subjects (Pathway to Success, Management Solutions for a Changing World, Marketing, Economics for Managers, Creativity and Innovation for Business, Unlocking Your Leadership Potential) are identical to every other ICMS Bachelor of Business stream, with event-specific specialisation subjects layered on top.

Electives are unusually broad for a specialist events degree: students can pull units from fashion, tourism, entrepreneurship, hospitality and sports, letting someone interested in, say, fashion week production build a genuinely tailored transcript rather than a fixed events-only pathway. That flexibility matters in an industry where career paths fork wildly: corporate conference production looks nothing like festival logistics or luxury wedding planning, and ICMS's elective spread acknowledges that rather than forcing one generic events curriculum on everyone.

The course runs 12 core subjects, 8 specialisation subjects, 4 electives and 2 WIL subjects across three year levels, with a typical full load of 6 to 8 subjects a year.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Creativity and Innovation for Business; Unlocking Your Leadership Potential
Level 200: Event Design and Production; Event Marketing and Sponsorship; Risk Management for Events; electives (fashion, tourism, entrepreneurship, hospitality or sports); Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Event Management; Festival and Major Event Operations; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (event industry placement)

name: Bachelor of Fashion and Global Brand Management
description:
This degree runs a slightly leaner elective load than most ICMS undergraduate degrees (26 subjects total, split across 12 core business units, 6 fashion specialisation subjects, 6 electives and 2 Work Integrated Learning subjects worth up to 600 placement hours), built specifically to prepare students for brand, retail and visual merchandising roles across the global fashion and luxury sector rather than design or garment construction, which ICMS explicitly doesn't teach here. It's a business degree with a fashion industry lens, not a fashion design degree with business units bolted on, and that distinction matters for anyone comparing it against TAFE or fashion-college design programs.

Specialisation content covers how fashion and luxury brands are built and managed, visual merchandising strategy, and the retailing and marketing techniques used across both physical stores and the now-dominant online fashion retail channel. Entry requires a Band 2 in English and one other subject at HSC level (Mathematics Standard 2, Business Studies, Economics among the accepted options), a relatively accessible bar reflecting the degree's practical, industry-facing positioning rather than an academically selective one.

Graduates go on to brand management, visual merchandising, retail buying and marketing roles; the degree's own careers material name-checks boutique brand management and online fashion retail marketing specifically as target outcomes.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Business Law; Accounting Fundamentals
Level 200: Fashion and Luxury Brand Management; Visual Merchandising; Retail Management; electives; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Global Fashion Marketing; Digital Fashion Retailing; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (fashion/retail industry placement, up to 600 hours combined with WIL 1)

name: Bachelor of International Hotel and Resort Management
description:
This is one of ICMS's founding disciplines. The college began as a hotel and hospitality training institution before broadening into general business degrees, and the hotel and resort management program still carries that institutional memory in the depth of its industry relationships. The course structure runs 12 core subjects, 8 specialisation subjects, 4 electives and 2 Work Integrated Learning subjects, with the WIL component covering up to two trimesters (about nine months combined) of paid or supervised internship placement, commonly inside branded international hotel groups with a Sydney or regional NSW presence.

Specialisation content covers rooms division and front office operations, food and beverage management, revenue management and resort operations specifically (as distinct from urban hotel management), reflecting the realities of Australia's resort sector along the coast and in regional tourism hubs. Electives pull from marketing, tourism, entrepreneurship, event management and sport, so students can shape the degree toward luxury resort management, conference and events, or broader hospitality group leadership depending on where they want to end up.

Graduates commonly move into hotel management trainee programs with international chains, a pathway ICMS has cultivated for decades given its origins, though the degree equally supports resort-specific and boutique property careers less common among city-based hospitality programs.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Introduction to Hospitality Operations; Accounting Fundamentals
Level 200: Rooms Division Management; Food and Beverage Management; Resort Operations; Revenue Management; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Hospitality Management; International Hotel Brand Management; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (hotel/resort industry placement)

name: Bachelor of International Tourism and Hospitality Management
description:
Where ICMS's Hotel and Resort Management degree leans into property-level operations, this program takes a wider destination and industry-management view: tourism policy, destination marketing, and cross-sector hospitality management alongside the hotel operations content shared across the college's tourism-adjacent degrees. It follows the same 12 core, 8 specialisation, 4 elective, 2 WIL subject structure as ICMS's other undergraduate business degrees, with the WIL placements often arranged with tourism boards, travel operators, or hospitality groups rather than exclusively hotel front desks.

Sydney and the broader NSW coast give this degree a genuinely useful backyard for its subject matter. International arrivals through Sydney Airport, cruise ship tourism through Sydney Harbour, and the Northern Beaches tourism economy that ICMS's own Manly campus sits inside all provide accessible, real-world case material that a program based somewhere without a comparable tourism economy would have to teach more abstractly.

Graduates typically head into destination marketing organisations, travel and tour operators, tourism policy roles with state or local government, or hospitality group management, a broader spread of outcomes than the hotel-specific degree, reflecting its wider industry-management framing.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Introduction to Tourism Systems; Creativity and Innovation for Business
Level 200: Destination Marketing; Tourism Policy and Planning; Hospitality Operations Management; Sustainable Tourism; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Tourism Management; International Tourism Trends; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (tourism/hospitality industry placement)

name: Bachelor of Property (Development, Investment and Valuation)
Master of Business Administration
description:
ICMS's MBA is structured as 12 subjects of coursework plus two Work Integrated Learning subjects, an Action Learning Project and a Professional Placement, rather than the thesis-heavy research pathway some MBAs default to. The college pitches it explicitly around leadership development ('mastery of leadership' is the phrase ICMS itself uses), with a people-first management focus running through the core subjects rather than treating leadership as a single bolted-on unit near the end.

Delivery mixes small lectures, tutorials and workshops with an emphasis on industry research, and units are also available online for students who can't attend the Manly campus full-time, a flexibility that matters given a chunk of the MBA cohort is working while studying. Full-time completion runs two years, and international graduates become eligible for post-study work visas of up to five years, a detail that matters enormously to the significant international contingent in ICMS's postgraduate programs generally.

The Action Learning Project asks students to work through a real strategic problem, typically sourced from their own employer or an industry partner, while the Professional Placement adds direct workplace experience for students who haven't already accumulated substantial industry tenure.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Leadership and Personal Development; Managerial Economics; Accounting for Decision Making
Trimester 2: Marketing Management; Organisational Behaviour; Corporate Finance
Trimester 3: Strategic Management; Business Research Methods; elective
Trimester 4: Global Business Environment; Operations and Supply Chain Management; elective
Trimester 5: Action Learning Project (Work Integrated Learning); Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Trimester 6: Professional Placement (Work Integrated Learning); MBA capstone

name: Master of Event Management
description:
This postgraduate degree builds on ICMS's undergraduate strength in event management, aimed at career-changers or industry professionals wanting a formal management qualification behind existing events experience rather than school leavers starting from scratch. Like ICMS's other masters, it combines dense coursework with two Work Integrated Learning subjects totalling 600 hours, and students already working in relevant event roles can apply for recognition of prior learning against that placement requirement rather than repeating hours they've effectively already logged professionally.

Content goes deeper into strategic event portfolio management, major event bidding and delivery, and event risk and crisis management than the undergraduate degree's more operational focus, appropriate for a cohort that in many cases already knows how to run an event and is here to learn how to manage an events business or a major event program at a strategic level. ICMS's Sydney location again does real work here, with access to major event case studies (Vivid Sydney, New Year's Eve on the Harbour, international sporting fixtures) that a program elsewhere would have to teach at a further remove.

Graduates typically move into senior event management roles, festival and major event directorships, or corporate event portfolio management within larger organisations.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Strategic Event Management; Event Marketing and Sponsorship; Managerial Economics
Trimester 2: Major Event Bidding and Delivery; Event Risk and Crisis Management; Research Methods
Trimester 3: Financial Management for Events; elective; Work Integrated Learning 1
Trimester 4: Event Portfolio Management; Global Event Trends; Work Integrated Learning 2 (or RPL pathway); capstone project

name: Master of International Business
description:
ICMS's Master of International Business is built the same way most of its postgraduate degrees are: dense coursework paired with a genuine industry placement rather than a token internship. Students complete two Work Integrated Learning subjects worth 600 hours combined, working inside an actual organisation on real business problems, and anyone already employed in a relevant industry role can apply for recognition of prior learning against that requirement instead of duplicating hours they've already put in at work.

The degree covers trade and finance, international economics, accounting, marketing and people management, aimed at giving graduates from non-business undergraduate backgrounds (and there are plenty in ICMS's international cohort) a genuinely broad management skillset rather than a narrow specialisation. ICMS leans on its Manly campus location and small class sizes to run the program with more direct staff contact than a large city university's equivalent masters, which shows up in seminar-style teaching rather than large lecture theatres.

Most students take two years full-time, and the international business framing suits ICMS's own student demographic well: a large share of the cohort comes from overseas and returns home, or moves into export/import and multinational management roles in Sydney, after graduating.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Global Business Environment; Managerial Economics; International Trade and Finance
Trimester 2: International Marketing; Cross-Cultural Management; Accounting for Managers
Trimester 3: Human Resource Management in a Global Context; Strategic Management; elective
Trimester 4: Work Integrated Learning 1 (600-hour placement, part 1); Research Methods
Trimester 5: Work Integrated Learning 2 (placement continued); International Business Strategy capstone
Trimester 6: Global Supply Chain Management; final elective
